featured_reviews.name: Sanjana Bhunia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been a student at IITians Science Point for the past three years. I appeared for NEET in both 2024 and 2025, and all my preparation was done entirely through this institute.

In my honest opinion, success in competitive exams like NEET and JEE depends majorly on the student. Teachers play a significant but partial role—around 20–30%—by guiding students with the syllabus, teaching effective methods, and providing practice questions. However, the rest is entirely up to the student—how they absorb information, manage their time, simplify complex concepts for themselves, and stay consistent in their efforts.

I say this from personal experience. Scoring 94% in class 10 gave me confidence, but in my first NEET attempt, I secured a rank of 1.16 lakh. That was a reality check. Being a good student in school doesn’t guarantee continued success unless you evolve with the pressure and expectations that follow. Some students handle that pressure well, others may not—but your journey ultimately depends on your dedication and how sincerely you work for your own future.

A genuine review of the coaching:

The faculty at IITians Science Point is top-notch. Every teacher is selected after rigorous testing and demo sessions. Most of them come from prestigious backgrounds—doctors, IITians, NITians, and other reputed institutions. Their focus is not just on completing the syllabus but on ensuring students truly understand the concepts and can solve problems confidently.

Weekly tests are taken very seriously here. Because there are multiple tests, certain types of questions are often repeated, which helps students recognize and learn from their past mistakes. Batches are well-organized, and the regular lectures keep the momentum going throughout the year.

Despite the vast syllabus, the teachers make sure it is covered on time, with proper conceptual clarity. Special mention to Imtiyaz Sir—the head and physics faculty—who creates a very supportive environment. He not only helps us academically but also personally guides us through challenges and stands by us at every step.

For students who miss any topics, revision sessions are provided after the syllabus is completed. The coaching center is continuously working on improving all aspects of its functioning to provide the best possible support.

In the end, it's your own hard work that will define your success. No system is perfect—but with the right support and your determination, you can definitely move closer to your goal.

featured_reviews.name: Aangi Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honest Review by Aangi Jain – BW Batch, NEET 2025 Aspirant

I’m Aangi Jain from the BW Batch, and I appeared for NEET 2025 after three years of preparation with ISP. Based on my experience, I can confidently say that ISP not only teaches the syllabus thoroughly but also provides valuable post-NEET counseling guidance from highly experienced experts — something that most institutes don’t offer.

The faculty at ISP is top-notch, including qualified doctors, IITians, and NITians. The support staff is also very helpful and always ready to assist students when needed. One thing I truly appreciate is the institute's consistency in conducting weekly tests. No matter what, the tests are held regularly, and detailed post-test analysis is shared. This helps students understand their mistakes and work on continuous improvement.

Honestly speaking, success in NEET is a 50-50 partnership between the institute and the student. Teachers do their job — they teach, solve doubts, and guide — but at the end of the day, it’s up to the student to put in the self-study hours.

Sadly, I’ve seen some students who were not serious about their studies or future careers blaming and even bullying teachers online. These are often the same students who were regularly scolded by faculty and staff for poor performance. Frankly, I believe this is just a way to gain sympathy from their parents for not doing well academically.

I’d like to personally thank Imtiyaz Sir, who has always supported and encouraged me throughout my preparation. Yes, he might be late by 15–30 minutes sometimes, but has anyone considered why? Maybe he was handling a previous class that ran overtime, or he was in a meeting with a student’s parents discussing their academic performance. These things are part of the dedication and responsibility he takes on.

The internet should not be a platform for venting frustration against teachers or an institute just because you couldn’t perform well. If a student truly wants to succeed, they will — regardless of the challenges.

This is an honest and heartfelt review — not influenced by any gifts or rewards from ISP. I had a good NEET 2025 attempt and am currently in the Medical Admission Counseling process, aiming for a Government BDS seat. I’m hopeful and confident.

So yes: ISP + A Hardworking Student = SUCCESS
